answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Farrier shoeing register with veterinary college attestation, each register entry is horses shod and logged with the veterinary college, so a farm must shoe a hundred real horses becomes the price of admission, and the glacier is that the price is charged per identity. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The meadow is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The relic is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
